Definition: from G3844 and ὀτρύνω (to spur); to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility):--stir up.
BiblicalUsage: Parotryno means to stir up, to urge along, to spur to hostility. It appears once, in Acts 13:50, where the Jews stir up the devout and honourable women and the chief men of Antioch, and raise persecution against Paul and Barnabas and expel them out of their coasts.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the stirring up at Antioch shows how persecution starts: not with a mob, but with respectable people urged on by those who feel threatened.
